risks: The docs project currently depends ONLY on cats-effect, not on any Grackle module. Any compiled mdoc-inline example or new docs example source will fail to compile until build.sbt adds .dependsOn(core.jvm, circe.jvm, generic.jvm, doobiepg). This is the single biggest build-readiness risk; prefer snip-existing/snip-new-in-demo over mdoc-inline where possible to limit the blast radius.

snip-from-test-source requires editing many test files to add `// #tag` markers. The Output.snip extractor takes EVERYTHING between two lines containing the tag, so tags must bracket exactly the intended region and the region must be self-explanatory out of context (test files often interleave assertions). Mis-placed tags will silently include/exclude lines. Each new tag must be verified against the current source line ranges (the briefs cite line numbers that may drift).

Output.snip reads files via a RELATIVE path (Path.of(path)) resolved against the mdoc/site working directory (the repo root, as the existing demo snips prove). Snipping from modules/*/src/test/scala and modules/docs/src/main relies on the same cwd; if Laika/mdoc runs from a different base the relative paths break. Verify the working directory before authoring many test-source snips.

DB-dependent examples (SQL how-tos, paging, interfaces/unions, jsonb, mutations-SQL, nested effects) must be snip-only or compile-only and MUST NOT be executed at docs-build time (no live DB during site build). They are all marked snip-existing precisely so no DB is needed; do not convert any of them to runnable mdoc blocks.

Scala 2 vs 3 divergence: generic derivation, the schema/doc interpolators, and Like live in scala-2/scala-3 source roots. mdoc compiles under one Scala version per docs build; examples that touch version-specific internals should snip the shared public API, not the per-version implementation, to avoid build breakage on the other axis.

The in-memory tutorial currently hand-maintains a Query-algebra ADT block and 'before/after' elaboration terms as plain (uncompiled) ```scala blocks. These can drift from the real source. The plan moves the authoritative ADT to reference/query-algebra.md (snipped), but if the tutorial keeps illustrative uncompiled snippets they remain a drift risk and should be clearly marked as illustrative.

The StarWars demo is simultaneously the in-memory tutorial AND the generic-derivation example. Reusing its snips across tutorial/in-memory-model.md and how-to/generic-derivation.md is intentional (minimizes new code) but means changes to the demo source affect multiple pages — keep tag regions stable.

Volume: this plan adds ~36 new pages plus tag edits across ~25 source files. Authoring is large; P0/P1 prioritization is provided so a first publishable cut (Getting Started + 3 tutorials + core how-tos + key references) can ship before the P2 long tail.

mkResponse/InternalError behaviour (internal errors raise into F rather than appearing as GraphQL errors) is subtle and easy to mis-document; the errors how-to and result-problem reference must state it explicitly to avoid implying internal errors come back as JSON.

No built-in Relay connection type and no built-in websocket/graphql-ws transport exist. The paging how-to and the serve-over-http/subscriptions pages must avoid implying ready-made helpers exist, or readers will look for APIs that aren't there.
crossCuttingNotes: Reuse over rewrite: the existing demo (StarWars generic, World SQL) is already snip-tagged and compiled; the three retained tutorials keep their current snips. New compiled example code is limited to three small files in modules/docs (quick-start, mutations+subscriptions, in-memory filtering) — everything else is snip-existing from demo or test sources, satisfying the 'minimize new code' constraint.

Snip strategy precedence used throughout: (1) snip-existing from demo (already tagged, compiled, no new deps) > (2) snip-existing from test sources (compiled, but need new // #tag markers; no docs-module dep needed since Output.snip reads raw files) > (3) snip-new compiled example in modules/docs (needs docs .dependsOn) > (4) mdoc-inline (compiled inline; needs docs .dependsOn; used sparingly for tiny schema/Result/Problem illustrations).

DB safety invariant: every example whose needsDb=true is snip-existing or compile-only and is never executed at site-build time. The site build only runs mdoc-inline blocks and the three new compiled modules/docs examples, all of which are DB-free.

Diátaxis discipline: Tutorials are end-to-end and runnable; How-to pages are task recipes that may snip DB-backed code; Concepts explain mechanisms (no exhaustive signatures); Reference pages are signature-dense and snip from main sources. Cross-links flow tutorial->how-to->reference and how-to->concepts.

Consolidation: the hand-maintained Query-algebra ADT and elaboration before/after currently inlined in in-memory-model.md are superseded by reference/query-algebra.md and concepts/compiler-elaboration.md (both snipped from real sources) to remove drift. The tutorial should link to them rather than duplicate.

Effects and composition appear in BOTH a How-to (task recipe) and a Concepts page (mechanism). This is deliberate Diátaxis separation, not duplication: the how-to shows the steps, the concept explains staging/batching. Keep the snipped code in the how-to and keep the concept prose-focused.
Every new section gets its own directory.conf for Laika nav ordering and a section title; the top-level docs/directory.conf is extended to order the five sections. CONTRIBUTING.md stays last.

Tag-naming convention for new snips: lowercase, hyphen/underscore, prefixed per file purpose (e.g. #world_elaborator, #composed_mapping, #circe_mapping, #scalars_leafmappings) to keep them greppable and avoid collisions, since Output.snip matches any line CONTAINING the tag string.
